videos.title: How Is Soap Made? (From Fat and Lye) 🧼
videos.description:
Soap is fat or oil mixed with lye, a chemical that burns skin. The reaction (saponification) turns them into soap and glycerin, with no lye left. Babylonians did it almost 5,000 years ago. Each soap molecule has a water-loving head and a grease-loving tail, which is how it cleans.
Bar soap or liquid soap? 👇

videos.title: How Is Cheese Made? (The Holes Are Bacteria Burps) 🧀
videos.description:
Milk plus good bacteria, then rennet makes it set like jelly. It's cut into cubes that squeeze out whey, pressed into wheels, salted and aged for months. In Swiss cheese, special bacteria burp gas bubbles that become the holes.
What's the best cheese on Earth? 👇

videos.title: How Is Coffee Made? (Beans Aren't Beans) ☕
videos.description:
Coffee beans are the seeds of a red fruit, the coffee cherry. Brazil grows the most. The seeds are dried green and smell like grass, then roasted around 220 °C for about 12 minutes until they crack like popcorn, which is when the coffee aroma is born.
How many coffees a day? 👇
